title: Files & Errors
short_description: Read and write files, handle errors.
bro_quote: Robust programs handle errors gracefully and persist data to disk—master both to build real applications.

subtopics.name: File Basics and Modes
subtopics.explanation:
• 📂 open(filename, mode) opens a file. Returns a file object.
  • 📝 Common modes: 'r' (read), 'w' (write), 'a' (append), 'x' (create).
  • ⚠️ 'w' mode overwrites the file if it exists! Be careful.
  • 🔒 Always close files with .close() or use with.

snippets.comment: Opening a file in different modes
snippets.code:
# Read mode
f = open("data.txt", "r")
# Write mode (creates or overwrites)
f = open("data.txt", "w")
# Append mode (adds to end)
f = open("data.txt", "a")
f.close()

subtopics.name: Writing Files
subtopics.explanation:
• 📝 .write() writes text to a file.
  • 🆕 'w' mode creates a new file or overwrites existing one.
  • 📄 .writelines() writes multiple lines at once.
  • 💾 Data stays in memory until file is closed.

snippets.code:
f = open("greeting.txt", "w")
f.write("Hello, World!\n")
f.write("Python is awesome!")
f.close()

subtopics.name: Reading Files
subtopics.explanation:
• 📖 .read() reads the entire file as one string.
  • 📋 .readline() reads one line at a time.
  • 📄 .readlines() reads all lines into a list.
  • 🔁 Loop through files directly: for line in file_object

snippets.code:
f = open("greeting.txt", "r")
content = f.read()
print(content)
f.close()

f = open("data.txt", "r")
lines = f.readlines()      # List of all lines
for line in lines:
    print(line.strip())
f.close()

subtopics.name: Appending to Files
subtopics.explanation:
• ➕ 'a' mode appends text without deleting existing content.
  • 🎯 Perfect for adding logs or new data to existing files.
  • 📍 Write position is at the end of the file.

snippets.code:
f = open("log.txt", "a")
f.write("New log entry\n")
f.write("Another entry\n")
f.close()

subtopics.name: The 'with' Statement
subtopics.explanation:
• 🤝 with automatically closes files when done. No need to call .close()
  • 🛡️ Safer than manual close — works even if errors occur.
  • ✨ Best practice for file handling in Python.

snippets.code:
with open("data.txt", "r") as f:
    content = f.read()
    print(content)
# File automatically closed here

with open("output.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write("Line 1\n")
    f.write("Line 2\n")
# File automatically closed

subtopics.name: Understanding Errors
subtopics.explanation:
• 💥 Errors (exceptions) stop your program if not handled.
  • 🏷️ Common errors: ZeroDivisionError, FileNotFoundError, ValueError, IndexError.
  • ⚠️ Error message tells you what went wrong and where.
  • 🔍 Use the error type to handle specific problems.

snippets.code:
# ZeroDivisionError
result = 10 / 0  # Error!
# FileNotFoundError
f = open("nonexistent.txt", "r")  # Error!
# ValueError
num = int("abc")  # Error!

subtopics.name: try/except Blocks
subtopics.explanation:
• 🛡️ try: contains code that might cause an error.
  • ✅ except: runs if an error occurs in the try block.
  • 🎯 Catch specific errors: except SpecificError:
  • ❌ Multiple except blocks for different error types.

subtopics.name: finally and else Blocks
subtopics.explanation:
• 🔄 finally: runs no matter what — error or no error. Great for cleanup.
  • ✅ else: runs only if NO error occurred.
  • 💡 Use finally for closing resources or cleanup tasks.

snippets.code:
try:
    result = 10 / 2
    print(result)
except ZeroDivisionError:
    print("Error!")
finally:
    print("Cleanup done!")

subtopics.name: Raising Custom Errors
subtopics.explanation:
• 🚨 raise keyword throws an error manually.
  • 🎯 Use raise ValueError(message) for custom errors.
  • 🔍 Great for validating user input or data.
  • 💡 Helps catch problems early in your program.

subtopics.name: Practical File and Error Handling
subtopics.explanation:
• 🏗️ Combine files and error handling for robust programs.
  • 📝 Always handle missing files and invalid input.
  • 💾 Use logging to save errors to a file for debugging.

questions: 1. Use the open() function to create a brand new text file in 'w' mode. (Opening file)
2. Write a single sentence into the text file you just opened. (Writing file)
3. Open an existing text file in 'r' mode and print its contents to the screen. (Reading file)
4. Open a text file in 'a' mode (append) to add a new line without deleting the old ones. (Appending)
5. Rewrite your file reading code to use the 'with' statement so it closes automatically. (With statement)
6. Deliberately try to divide a number by 0 and wrap it in a try/except block. (ZeroDivisionError)
7. Try to open a file that doesn't exist and catch the specific FileNotFoundError. (FileNotFoundError)
8. Write a try block that has two different except blocks for different types of errors. (Multiple excepts)
9. Add a finally block that prints 'Execution finished' regardless of whether an error happened. (Finally block)
10. Use the raise keyword to force a custom error if a user inputs a negative age. (Raising errors)
